Calculate Anomalies from a Baseline Mean

calc_anomaly.Rd

Calculates the anomaly of a variable relative to a user-specified baseline period. Returns a focused data frame containing only the year, the original value, the baseline mean used, and the resulting anomaly.

Usage

calc_anomaly(data, baseline_range, year_range = NULL, quiet = FALSE)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing at least year and value columns.

baseline_range

Numeric vector c(start, end) defining the period used to calculate the mean. This argument is required.

year_range

Optional numeric vector c(start, end) to filter the returned data. If NULL, returns all years in the input data.

quiet

Logical. If FALSE (default), prints the baseline mean to the console via a message.

Value

A focused data frame (tibble) with columns: year, value, baseline_mean, and anomaly.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Example 1: Using the native R pipe (|>)
sst_anom <- EA.data |>
  dplyr::filter(variable == "sst.month10", EAR == 0) |>
  calc_anomaly(baseline_range = c(1991, 2020))

# Example 2: Using base R subset() and assignment
physical_data <- subset(EA.data, variable == "t.deep" & EAR == 1)
deep_t_anom <- calc_anomaly(data = physical_data,
                            baseline_range = c(1995, 2015))

# View the clean result
head(deep_t_anom)
} # }
